answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-reputation bond: every new agent must lock a deposit before it can earn, and that deposit is slashed if peers prove fake activity. The bond works like a violet filter: most cheap hollow identities wash out, because creating thousands of them would cost thousands of deposits, while a single honest agent pays once and keeps working. A comet of fake accounts burns bright, then loses its stake, so attackers must keep paying to return. Honest participants recover their bond over time, so the cost falls on attackers, not on legitimate users.
